data.hypothesis: Reducing the block size from 256 to 128 doubles the CTA count at the official larger sizes while preserving one thread per target and all kernel calculations. This may improve scheduling, but smaller CTAs may also reduce efficiency; the aggregate baseline timing does not establish which effect dominates.
data.notes: Only the launch configuration changes, with the same three JSON keys and items_per_block equal to block. Require correctness validation for every supported size before comparing official timings. The baseline is valid and averages 0.0018526411283622502 seconds; no per-size timing breakdown is available, and this candidate has not been measured.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 128 while keeping shared_memory_bytes at 0; leave the kernel and its traversal, equations, and memory strategy unchanged.
